subject: Getting different results when random effects were in different order in my code

messages.author: b7d8701fe15f0b01
messages.subject: Getting different results when random effects were in different order in my code
parts:
Hi,
I am running a model with repeated measures for each person and three random effects.
My random effects are things like school and year.
So I have :
y ~Normal(theta, variance) where y is their weight
g(theta)=alpha+sum(beta_i)(x_i)+f(Z1)+f(Z2)+f(Z3), where (x_i)s are the fixed effect. Z1=school,Z2=year etc.

My code uses f(Zi,model="iid") for Z1,Z2,Z3, and the identifier for each case I have also included as f("personal_ID",model="iid).

Is it correct to assume the hyper parameters are the precisons for Z1,Z2 and Z3? I should not worry bout the personal_ID variable?

However, when I run the model with slight different ordering of f(Z1),f(Z2) and f(Z3), the posterior precisions for Z1,Z2,Z3 and the personal_ID variables differ greatly.

Is there any rules around the ordering of these within the R code?
Is my understanding of the posterior precisions correct?

Many thanks
